options_evaluated: 100% Post-Consumer Recycled (PCR) Polypropylene (PP) with structural ribbing
decisions.trade_off: Balancing mechanical durability and impact resistance (to prevent premature structural failure) against the embodied carbon footprint and end-of-life circularity of the polymer.
decisions.recommendation: 100% Post-Consumer Recycled (PCR) Polypropylene (PP) with structural ribbing
decisions.rationale: PCR PP dramatically reduces the product's carbon footprint compared to virgin engineering plastics. While PP has lower inherent tensile strength than ABS/PC, utilizing strategic internal ribbing restores the necessary structural integrity for a vacuum cleaner housing without adding significant weight or compromising recyclability.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the mechanical properties and supply chain reliability of certified PCR PP grades to verify they meet minimum impact resistance requirements for consumer appliances.

options_evaluated: Standardized stainless steel screws with brass threaded inserts
Snap-fits with integrated, visible release points
decisions.trade_off: Permanent joining (welding) minimizes part count and assembly time but prevents non-destructive disassembly, whereas mechanical fasteners facilitate repair but increase material complexity and assembly energy.
decisions.recommendation: Snap-fits with integrated, visible release points combined with standardized, thread-forming screws directly into the plastic
decisions.rationale: This hybrid approach eliminates the need for dissimilar material inserts (like brass) which contaminate plastic recycling streams, while still allowing technicians or consumers to easily disassemble the unit for repair or end-of-life material separation using common tools.
decisions.design_action: Verify disassembly guidelines and tool requirements against international eco-design standards, such as the EU Ecolabel criteria for vacuum cleaners, to ensure compliance.

decisions.trade_off: BLDC motors offer superior energy efficiency and a significantly longer operational lifespan, but rely on rare-earth magnets (neodymium) with high environmental extraction impacts; AC motors avoid rare-earths but have lower efficiency and wear out faster.
decisions.recommendation: High-efficiency Brushless DC (BLDC) motor utilizing certified recycled neodymium magnets
decisions.rationale: The lifetime energy savings and extended product lifespan (due to the absence of wearing brushes) far outweigh the initial environmental impact of magnet extraction, particularly when mitigating that impact by sourcing recycled magnet materials.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the availability of motor manufacturers that offer certified recycled magnet content or low-dysprosium magnet formulations in their standard BLDC catalogs.

options_evaluated: Active cooling via an auxiliary fan on the motor shaft
Passive cooling using extruded aluminum heat sinks
Bypass cooling utilizing the main vacuum working airflow
decisions.trade_off: Passive cooling requires substantial metal mass (aluminum extraction impact) but is silent and reliable, whereas utilizing the working airflow is highly material-efficient but requires complex filtration to prevent motor contamination.
decisions.recommendation: Bypass cooling utilizing the main vacuum working airflow, positioned post-HEPA filter
decisions.rationale: By routing the clean, filtered exhaust air over the motor, we eliminate the need for a heavy, resource-intensive aluminum heat sink or an auxiliary fan. This dual-use of the working airflow minimizes overall product mass and energy consumption.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the aerodynamic ducting layout to verify that the airflow path provides sufficient velocity over the motor housing without causing excessive static pressure drop.

options_evaluated: Modular cartridge-based architecture (separate motor, battery, and dust-bin modules)
Semi-modular layout with internal wire harnesses and plug connectors
decisions.trade_off: A modular cartridge architecture increases initial plastic material use due to double-walled enclosures for each module, but drastically reduces the barrier to user repair and component harvesting.
decisions.recommendation: Modular cartridge-based architecture for high-wear components (battery, motor, and filtration assembly)
decisions.rationale: Vacuum cleaners are frequently discarded due to single-point failures (e.g., a dead battery or clogged motor). Isolating these high-wear components into easily swappable, toolless cartridges ensures the rest of the product chassis remains in use, maximizing the utility of the embodied materials.
decisions.design_action: Investigate historical consumer return and repair data for vacuum cleaners to identify the top three failure modes and verify that the modular boundaries align with these components.

options_evaluated: Removable and interchangeable Lithium-ion battery pack
Cordless with an integrated, non-removable Lithium-ion battery
decisions.trade_off: Corded power avoids the high environmental and ethical impacts of battery manufacturing (lithium, cobalt) and degradation, but cordless models offer significantly higher user convenience, reducing the risk of premature product replacement due to perceived obsolescence.
decisions.recommendation: Removable and interchangeable Lithium-ion battery pack (utilizing Lithium Iron Phosphate - LFP chemistry)
decisions.rationale: A removable battery pack allows the consumer to replace only the degraded cells rather than disposing of the entire appliance. Choosing LFP chemistry avoids the ethical and environmental concerns of cobalt mining while offering a higher cycle life, offsetting the initial manufacturing footprint.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the feasibility of aligning the battery pack interface with an existing multi-brand battery alliance to allow consumers to share batteries across multiple household appliances.
